title: Queensland storms declared significant as claims tally passes 4500
full_text:
Queensland storms declared significant as claims tally passes 4500
Severe storms across southeast Queensland have been declared a significant event by the Insurance Council of Australia.
Insurers have received about 4670 claims, mostly for fallen trees and branches, damaged roofs and fences, and water entering homes.
“Severe damage has so far been confined to a small number of properties,” ICA said today.
Wind speeds equivalent to a category 1 cyclone struck Queensland’s Logan area on Wednesday, and torrential rain then drenched the southeast. Last night, severe storms swept across Toowoomba, the Gold Coast, Brisbane and the Sunshine Coast.
The Bureau of Meteorology warns this is expected to continue today, bringing destructive wind, large hail and heavy rain. Flood warnings are in place for the Logan River.
Insurers have teams in affected communities, and the significant event declaration escalates and prioritises industry responses, with real-time tracking of claim volumes and estimated losses.
Insurers will engage with government, emergency services and recovery agencies to help affected residents.
ICA says since 2022 Logan has been affected by eight declared events, not counting the latest storms, and the Logan-Albert River is one of 24 catchments identified for priority flood defence infrastructure.
“Every household affected by these storms is dealing with real cost and stress ... The sooner a claim is lodged, the sooner insurers can start helping people get back on their feet,” ICA CEO Andrew Hall said.
"What we're seeing in Logan is a reminder of how frequently severe weather is impacting Australian communities and why we need to keep investing in measures that reduce that risk."
IAG says two response vehicles are stationed at the Browns Plains Bunnings car park, supporting customers with claims and recovery assistance.
The insurer's teams of assessors and partner builders have scheduled more than 384 emergency make safe repairs since the storm outbreak last week.
